Definition: from G3844 and G1776; to harass further, i.e. annoy:--trouble.
BiblicalUsage: Parenochleo means to trouble, to harass, to annoy. It appears once, in Acts 15:19, where James gives sentence at Jerusalem: we trouble not them, which from among the Gentiles are turned to God.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the council's wisdom was restraint: do not trouble the Gentiles with a yoke they were never meant to carry.
